title: Score-instrument separation must be observed, not self-reported
boundedQuestion: Does the current KB2 bird instrument compute morphology from score data, or does it hide species presets behind a score selector?
existingFailureMechanism: The workbench displays speciesSwitchPresent=false and finalVerticesStored=false, but those values are returned by the instrument itself. A hidden identity branch or ignored morphology slot can keep the same self-report and still violate the architecture.
hypothesis: A claim-scoped metamorphic gate will distinguish a genuinely score-driven instrument from a self-reporting preset selector: identity-only changes preserve geometry, morphology changes alter geometry, identical input replays byte-equivalently, unknown slots reject, and the instrument contains no known species literal.

metamorphicRelations.inputChange: Change identity labels and instance id only
Change bill-axis length and body-section width in score only

metamorphicRelations.requiredOutputRelation: Build rejects instead of silently selecting a preset
No known object-specific species literal appears

applicability: Instrument-score systems claiming that object-specific knowledge lives in the score while the instrument contains only category capabilities. It does not validate visual fidelity, anatomy, motion naturalness, or user acceptance.
comparisonToCurrentRules: R2 and N42 already prohibit self-approval and require evidence for claims. The novel executable increment is the score-instrument-specific observable relation set; it replaces a tautological boolean with behavior that can be falsified.
